Fingerprinting and matching signing payloads for transactions, gossip, shreds, TLS, ping, pong, bundle, and event messages.

# Purpose
This file implements the payload fingerprinting logic for the keyguard. It checks untrusted signing requests and maps each request to a payload class such as `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_TXN`, `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_GOSSIP`, `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_REPAIR`, `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_PRUNE`, `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_SHRED`, `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_TLS_CV`, `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_PING`, `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_PONG`, `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_BUNDLE`, and `FD_KEYGUARD_PAYLOAD_EVENT`. The code uses fixed-size checks, prefix checks, and small field inspections to detect the message type from the raw bytes and the signing type. The main entry point is [`fd_keyguard_payload_match`](<#fd_keyguard_payload_match>), which combines all match tests and returns the matching payload flag.

The file focuses on avoiding false negatives when it identifies transaction messages and other supported signing payloads. The helper [`fd_keyguard_payload_matches_txn_msg`](<#fd_keyguard_payload_matches_txn_msg>) performs the most detailed parsing, including transaction header checks, size limits, and compact-u16 address count decoding. The other helpers use direct size and prefix checks for message families such as gossip, repair, TLS `CertificateVerify`, ping, pong, bundle, event, prune data, and shred payloads. The code is written as a set of `FD_FN_PURE` functions so it can be used as a deterministic first-line filter before later authorization checks.
